summary: Open-core Chinese discrete-manufacturing MES (FastAPI + Tortoise ORM/aerich + React, default branch develop) whose OEE has a performance term that is always 100 percent and an 8-hour-per-day hardcoded denominator, has no device acquisition in the open tier (only an HTTP mock edge POC), uses a DeepSeek-based bounded AI layer with no Anthropic code, and exposes two unauthenticated /api/debug routes that return rows across all tenants.

d1_oee.formula: riveredge-backend/src/apps/kuaizhizao/services/equipment_oee_service.py: A = actual_runtime / (days_in_window * 8) * 100; P = (actual_qty * std_time_per_unit) / actual_runtime * 100 where std_time_per_unit = actual_runtime / actual_qty, so P is identically 100 whenever qty and runtime are both > 0; Q = qualified_qty / actual_qty * 100; OEE = A * P * Q / 10000 (percent units). Inputs are approved ReportingRecord rows (work_hours, reported_quantity, qualified_quantity) matched to equipment by device_info JSON keys equipment_id or equipment_code (no foreign key).
d1_oee.storage: No OEE table or snapshot model in the open repo. OEE is computed on request from reporting records and nothing is persisted.
gaps: Performance rate is algebraically 100 whenever qty and runtime are both positive, because std_time_per_unit is derived from the same runtime and quantity. The code's own TODO admits standard time is not taken from routing, so OEE effectively reduces to A * Q.
Availability denominator is hardcoded as working_days * 8 hours, ignoring shifts, calendars, planned stops and holidays.
Availability uses manually reported work_hours from reporting records, not machine state time. It is not linked to EquipmentStatusMonitor or StationOperationDowntime.
Clamping is to [0,100] percent units, not [0,1] as in the benchmark, and min/max clamping silently hides out-of-range inputs.

Each calculate_equipment_oee call loads all approved reporting records for the tenant and window, then filters in Python. list_equipment_oee calls it once per equipment, so the cost is equipment times records with no equipment filter in the query.
list_equipment_oee and get_equipment_oee_trend catch Exception and return zeros with an error string, so a failed calculation looks like 0 percent OEE.
A window shorter than 24 hours gives planned_runtime 0 and availability 0 because working_days uses integer days.

d2_downtime.model: Point-in-time status rows (EquipmentStatusMonitor) plus an append-only transition log (EquipmentStatusHistory with from_status, to_status, status_changed_at). Equipment.status holds the current value and is_online is a separate boolean. Downtime is a separate StationOperationDowntime event table (reason_code, started_at, nullable ended_at meaning still paused), entered by operators. EquipmentFault tracks fault tickets with response SLA fields. There is no state-interval table and no ISO 22400 reason taxonomy.
schema_fields: apps_kuaizhizao_equipment_status_monitors: tenant_id, equipment_id, equipment_uuid, equipment_code, status (VARCHAR 50, default 正常), is_online, runtime_hours, temperature, pressure, vibration, other_parameters (JSON), data_source (default manual), monitored_at
apps_kuaizhizao_equipment_status_histories: tenant_id, equipment_id, equipment_uuid, from_status, to_status, status_changed_at, changed_by, reason
apps_kuaizhizao_station_operation_downtimes: tenant_id, work_order_id, operation_id, reason_code, reason_label, started_at, ended_at (nullable), operator_id, operator_name
apps_kuaizhizao_equipment_faults: fault_no, equipment_id, fault_type, fault_level, status (待处理, 处理中, 已修复, 已关闭), reported_at, response_minutes, response_due_at
gaps: No canonical running/idle/fault/offline enum. status is free-text Chinese with max_length only and no choices validation. Offline exists only as is_online = false.
No machine-state interval table. Durations per state must be derived from status history rows; no computed run or down time per state.
Downtime is operator-entered (station_operation_downtime), not machine-sourced, and reason_code is a free string with no taxonomy.
get_realtime_status_list in services/equipment_status_monitor_service.py calls get_latest_status once per equipment, an N+1 pattern.
Realtime runtime_hours is returned as null when the stored value is 0.00, because the code uses a truthiness check.
No telemetry ingestion path exists in the open repo. Status is set through the manual update API.

protocols: HTTP push (kuaivision edge-agent POC, mock data only)
d3_device.edge_arch: riveredge-backend/src/apps/kuaivision/edge-agent/agent.py is a Python 3 httpx client that polls config, sends heartbeats, and uploads batches, with a local SQLite buffer (buffer_db_path). It runs mock thickness and step pipelines driven by config.yaml mock_* keys. It is not Rust. Its README says the source lives in the private kuaigeyun-pro repo, yet the file is in this public repo.
d3_device.write_guard: No machine-write guard for devices was found in open source. The edge endpoints under /api/v1/apps/kuaivision/edge/{token}/... are exempt from the write-gate middleware and need no user JWT. The device_token sits in the URL path.
gaps: No MQTT, OPC UA, Modbus or serial acquisition code found in the open repo. README lists 快数采 (acquisition) and 快连接 as Pro.
The edge agent is a POC: mock_thickness_values and mock_step_missing_last generate fake readings, and there is no real device driver.
Device token in the URL path is recorded by proxies and access logs, unlike header-based auth.
aiomqtt and influxdb-client are declared in riveredge-backend/pyproject.toml, but no consumer was located in the directories inspected.

d4_data_model.hierarchy: Tenant (tenant_id on every BaseModel row) > factory and master data (apps/master_data) > workstation (StationShiftHandover.workstation_id) > equipment (apps/kuaizhizao/models/equipment.py) > work order (models/work_order.py) > work order operation (models/work_order_operation.py) > reporting records. Downtime rows reference work_order_id and operation_id.
d4_data_model.shift_model: StationShiftHandover (apps/kuaizhizao/models/station_shift_handover.py): per-workstation handover with shift_start, shift_end, planned_qty, completed_qty, unqualified_qty, downtime_minutes, andon_count and summary_json. Shift definitions are not in this model; a working_hours_configs API exists under core/api but was not read.
d4_data_model.telemetry_schema: EquipmentStatusMonitor table: status, is_online, runtime_hours, temperature, pressure, vibration, other_parameters JSON, data_source, monitored_at. Indexed on tenant_id, equipment_id, equipment_uuid, status, is_online, monitored_at, created_at. Plain PostgreSQL through Tortoise; no TimescaleDB hypertable found.
d4_data_model.tenancy: tenant_id is on every row via infra/models/base.py, but it is declared null=True with db_index, so the database does not enforce NOT NULL. The OEE service scopes equipment lookups by tenant_id and raises NotFoundError for other tenants (404 behavior). The /api/debug routes break the isolation rule.

d5_api.versioning: All routers use the /api/v1 prefix (server/main.py). No v2 or header-based versioning was found.
d5_api.realtime: Socket.IO (core/services/realtime/socketio_server.py) wrapped around the FastAPI app. connect requires a JWT in auth, then joins tenant-scoped and personal rooms (core/services/realtime/channels.py). Default REALTIME_BACKEND is noop, so realtime is off unless configured. A Centrifugo publisher also exists.
d5_api.envelope: create_success_response in core/utils/response_helper.py returns {success, data, timestamp, plus optional message and code}. infra.responses defines StandardResponse and PaginatedResponse.
d5_api.auth: JWT via python-jose. Access tokens default to 30 minutes. JWT_SECRET_KEY defaults to the placeholder 'your-secret-key-here-change-in-production'. Open API and superadmin tokens have separate secret settings that fall back to the JWT key.

d6_ai.model: DeepSeek by default (deepseek-v4-flash at https://api.deepseek.com, OpenAI-compatible), with an OpenAI provider spec. No Anthropic or claude-sonnet-4-6 code was found.
gaps: core/ai/agent_runner.py caps the tool loop at MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 6 with tool_choice auto. RBAC is enforced in the tool executor, which was not read.
Tools are registered from app manifests with an optional permission string (core/ai/tool_registry.py). Whether any tool writes data was not verified, so read-only status is unproven.
No AI-specific rate limiter was found. core/ai/middleware.py only logs tenant, user, route and latency.
The audit covers request metadata only (tenant, user, route, latency), not prompts, tool arguments or tool results.
AiRuntimeConfig.load(tenant_id) is per tenant, which is good, but tool-level tenant scoping is not evidenced in the files read.

d7_quality.tests: pytest with pytest-asyncio in strict mode. tests/ split into apps, core and infra. tests/apps/kuaizhizao covers column filters, customer pool ownership, 8D gate, HTML-to-PDF isolation, logistics and supplier scoring. No tests found for OEE, equipment status, downtime, shift or equipment-endpoint tenant isolation.
d7_quality.ci: No CI config found. The repo root has no .github directory. README says open-source CI runs scan_pro_oss_layout.py. riveredge-backend/scripts holds scan_permission_bypass.py, scan_manifest_permissions.py and scan_timezone_contract.py, which are not wired to any CI found.
d7_quality.migrations: Tortoise ORM with aerich 0.7.1, not Alembic. riveredge-backend/migrations/models has about 1983 migration files. The sampled file defines both upgrade and downgrade, so down migrations are provided. Unique and db_index constraints are added via SQL in migration files. The file count suggests heavy schema churn.
security_flags: /api/debug/batches and /api/debug/materials (server/main.py ~lines 537-553) have no auth dependency and no tenant filter. Cross-tenant data exposure.
JWT_SECRET_KEY placeholder default and database defaults postgres/postgres apply when env is not overridden.
Edge device_token is passed in the URL path; edge endpoints are exempt from the write gate and user JWT.
Base tenant_id is nullable (infra/models/base.py:53), so rows can exist without an organization.
License metadata: GitHub API reports NOASSERTION ('Other') while README states Apache 2.0. Verify LICENSE before reuse.
d7_quality.last_active: Default branch is develop. Last push 2026-10-21T00:41:58Z, metadata updated 2026-11-05.

adopt: Transition log pattern: EquipmentStatusHistory (from_status, to_status, status_changed_at) written alongside the current status.
Open-ended downtime rows: StationOperationDowntime.ended_at is nullable to mean still paused.
Per-workstation shift handover summary with planned, completed, unqualified qty and downtime_minutes (StationShiftHandover).
Socket.IO connect-time JWT check with tenant and personal room names (core/services/realtime/socketio_server.py, channels.py).
Bounded LLM tool loop (MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 6) and per-tool permission strings in ToolRegistry.
Per-tenant AI runtime config loaded from the database (AiRuntimeConfig.load(tenant_id)).
Pinning risky dependencies exactly in pyproject (playwright==1.63.0, tortoise-orm==0.21.1), with the reason written next to each pin.
avoid: OEE performance term that is always 100 percent, and the hardcoded 8 hours per day availability denominator.
OEE computed on request with per-equipment full scans and silent zero-fill on exceptions.
Free-text status with no enum or choices validation.
Placeholder JWT secret and postgres/postgres defaults as fallbacks.
Device token in the URL path, and an HTTP mock edge agent with no real drivers.
Nullable tenant_id on the base model.
Migration sprawl of about 1983 aerich files.
differentiate: Compute OEE per ISO 22400: availability from machine state intervals (running, idle, fault, offline) rather than manual work_hours, performance from ideal cycle time per routing operation, quality from good over total, clamped to [0,1] with out-of-range inputs flagged rather than silently clamped.
Persist OEE snapshots per machine and shift with source timestamps, so trends do not recompute from raw reports.
Enforce organization_id NOT NULL and check tenant at the DB boundary, with cross-org returning 404 on every path including debug and admin routes.
Machine connectivity through a Rust edge gateway over read-only MQTT and OPC UA, outbound-only, with idempotent Kafka consumers. This repo has only a Python HTTP POC.
AI limited to read-only tools on claude-sonnet-4-6, rate-limited per tenant, with full tool-call audit. This repo logs request metadata only.
Telemetry in TimescaleDB hypertables. This repo uses plain indexed PostgreSQL tables with no time-series partitioning.
